Definition: from G575 and G2749; to be reserved; figuratively, to await:--be appointed, (be) laid up.
BiblicalUsage: To be laid up, reserved, waiting. A crown of righteousness is laid up for Paul in 2 Timothy 4:8, and the hope laid up in heaven in Colossians 1:5. Hebrews 9:27 turns the word sober: it is appointed unto men once to die, but after this the judgment. And the fearful servant in Luke 19:20 kept his pound laid up in a napkin.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the word asks me what I have laid up, and where. A crown, a hope, a judgment — all three are laid up and waiting. The servant's pound was laid up too, and it earned him nothing, because he laid it up in fear instead of putting it to work. What is reserved for me depends on what I do with what was given me.
